subject: Cyclone service degradation — executive brief & customer commitments
messages:
From: Elena Korhonen <elena.k@cyclone.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate / 503s across inference endpoints (Cyclone courtyard)

Camila —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 5xx errors and latency across our inference endpoints around 06:50 PST. Error rate peaked around 18% for ~10 minutes; customers are reporting timeouts and retries. We attached a short log excerpt and a link to our internal dashboard (ops@cyclone.io).

Observed:
- Increased 5xx (mostly 503) across the primary eu-west and us-west routes
- CPU/GPU utilization on our side shows no saturation; we see repeated request retries from the Redwood API (X-Req-Id traces included)
- SLO impact: increased tail latency and failed responses for production traffic

Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on Redwood's side? We need immediate ETA and any mitigation steps you can take to reduce customer impact. Cyclone has an upcoming peak at 09:30 PST — if this persists we'll need a timeline to present to execs.

Attaching: log_excerpt.txt (snippet), dashboard link.

Thanks —
Elena
Elena Korhonen
Head of Platform Reliability, Cyclone.io

Subject: Internal: quick technical assessment + mitigation proposal (Cyclone)

Folks —

Quick notes from the infra triage that I wanted to surface before the bridge:
- Symptom: short-lived spike in request queuing within our GPU serving layer, causing elevated tail latency and 503s when request timeouts exceeded the proxy window. No host-level OOMs observed.
- Likely proximate causes: a) sudden burst from Cyclone traffic pattern (originating from a scheduler job we see at 06:47 PST) + b) a kernel-level scheduling regression on specific driver/kernel combo we rolled last week (limited to a subset of nodes).

Immediate mitigation I propose (can be executed now):
1) Route Cyclone's production traffic to a reserved warm pool for 30–60 minutes (reduces contention) — will require a short config push and quick warm-up, ETA ~15 minutes after approval.
2) Toggle prefix KV caching aggressively for Cyclone traffic to reduce token re-computation (config change, no infra restart) — immediate.
3) If routing is not acceptable, apply a temporary per-customer concurrency cap with graceful fallback to the smaller model variant (low-latency but lower throughput) — ETA ~20 minutes.

I’ve attached a live_metrics_snapshot.png and a proposed_rollforward.sh (ops script) for the team to review on the bridge. Recommend we run mitigation #1+2 immediately while we complete the full root cause analysis.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Serving Infrastructure | Redwood Inference

Subject: Cyclone status update (post-mitigation) — actions taken and next steps

Elena —

Thank you for joining the bridge earlier. Below is a concise summary of what happened, what we did, current status, and the commitments Redwood is making.

Summary / current status:
- Incident window: ~06:50–08:25 PST. Peak error rate ~18% (503s) for ~10 minutes.
- Root cause (preliminary): a simultaneous traffic burst from Cyclone plus a scheduling regression triggered on a small subset of nodes after last week
- Mitigations applied 08:10–08:25 PST: routing Cyclone traffic to a reserved warm pool + aggressive prefix KV caching. We also applied a temporary concurrency cap on a small fraction of requests to prevent cascading queue growth.
- Current metrics (as of 12:50 PST): error rate stable <0.5%, p99 latency within SLO, throughput returned to expected baseline.

Customer-facing commitments from Redwood:
1) RCA delivered by EOD 2027-03-10 (includes timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigation plan).
2) One-time service credit equivalent to 4 hours of dedicated capacity applied to your account (visible on next billing cycle).
3) Engineering follow-up: we will run a focused test with Cyclone traffic pattern in our staging environment; we propose a joint test window next week — will coordinate via your ops contact.

- diagnostic_snapshot_0308.json (detailed metrics dump)
- customer_impact_summary.pdf (concise impact & timeline for execs)

- If you need an earlier update or additional credits, reply here and I’ll escalate to our leadership.

We’re sorry for the disruption — thank you for the fast signal which helped us prioritize.

Best,
